Don't let them fool you when you hear DSL speed is ~tens of Mbps, and CAT6 speed is ~10 Gbps. Metal wires could guide THz waves, and people were dreaming and testing terabit DSL, using simple twisted pairs and such.
Well you might say these are so far sci-fi, but DSL has Gfast and MGfast (Multi-Gigabit fast) protocols, that can do up to 2 Gbps and 10 Gbps (?!) in short reach (~<400 m and ~< 100 m).

Cioffi2018: Terabit DSLs
https://doi.org/10.1109/MCOM.2018.1800597
Ahmed2025: Estimation of channel capacity in CAT6 cable with circular waveguide modeling for future THz communication systems
https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0233518
Here is a nice review on THz waveguides for communication:
Sohoo2024: Low Loss THz Waveguides and Its Potentials towards 6G Communication: A Brief Chronicle Review
https://www.ijeetc.com/show-240-1797-1.html

Gfast:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G.fast
MGfast: Oksman2019: MGFAST: A New Generation of Copper Broadband Access
https://doi.org/10.1109/MCOM.2019.1800844
Communication system papers always have so many acronyms..

A bt more on MGfast:
https://www.itu.int/hub/2021/08/up-to-8-gbit-s-broadband-with-new-itu-standard-mgfast/
The waveguide picture is from Markov2012: Practical Metal-Wire THz Waveguides
https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.2984
They only simulated the loss, and it's mostly dominated by bulk loss of the LDPE cladding, ~3 dB per meter

This is the OG metal wire THz guiding work:
Wang2004: Metal wires for terahertz wave guiding
https://www.nature.com/articles/nature03040
(also at:
https://bpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com/sites.brown.edu/dist/a/570/files/2024/07/waveguideNature.pdf)
The attraction of guiding with a bare wire is very low dispersion and propagation loss (it's even lower for higher freq??).
However it cannot bend much, when you see "can propagate on a slightly curved waveguide without a substantial increase in the loss", and no curvature stated, it basically means don't do it.
